question: Why wasn't the cbBTC/WETH position moved to Aerodrome, even though its interface showed a far higher APR than Uniswap?

facts.a: a staked Aerodrome position earns only AERO emissions; the fees go to voters
facts.b: the displayed emission APR is computed on liquidity in the active tick ±1 (about a 0.3% band); a ±40% position holds about 0.5% of it, about 4-6%/yr in AERO
facts.c: Uniswap at ±40% gives about 5-11%/yr in fees with no token to sell (AERO inflates about 10.9%/yr)
facts.d: the advantage exists only for ultra-narrow, actively managed positions, a class already falsified in late August
facts.e: verdict 08.09: no; Uniswap stays the venue for the wide position on this pair

reference: Checked on 08.09: on Aerodrome a position staked in the gauge earns only AERO emissions (the fees go to voters), and the displayed emission APR is computed on liquidity staked in the active tick ±1 tick, a band of about 0.3%. A ±40% position holds about 0.5% of that liquidity, so it would earn roughly 4 to 6% a year in AERO, a token with about 10.9% yearly inflation, against roughly 5 to 11% a year in fees on Uniswap with no token to sell. The LP crowd on Aerodrome sits about 10x tighter, so a wide position gets crumbs; the advantage exists only for ultra-narrow, actively managed positions, the class the project had falsified in late August. Verdict: no, Uniswap stays the venue for the wide position.
notes: Medium. Held-out batch 3 (2026-11-26), written by CC-Mac; review file ai/eval/review/heldout-batch-3.md.

question: What does an UNMAPPED verdict mean in the candidate funnel?

facts.a: the verdict when a ranked pool cannot be mapped to its on-chain address (token outside the dictionary of majors, or the token0/token1 sanity check disagrees); manual review, the funnel never guesses addresses
facts.b: exotic pairs without an ETH/BTC or stable leg are UNMAPPED by rule
facts.c: eligibility and OPEN proposals skip FAIL and UNMAPPED pools
facts.d: in the first full backfill (25.08) all 5 candidates were mapped, zero UNMAPPED

reference: The funnel validates pools from the DefiLlama ranking, and first maps each one to its on-chain address through a dictionary of known major tokens per network, factory.getPool and a sanity check of token0/token1. When a token is outside the dictionary or the sanity check disagrees, the verdict is UNMAPPED: the pool goes to manual review and the funnel never guesses an address or runs on silently wrong data. Exotic pairs without an ETH/BTC or stable leg are UNMAPPED by rule. Eligibility and OPEN proposals skip FAIL and UNMAPPED pools. In the first full backfill (25.08) all 5 candidates were mapped, zero UNMAPPED.

question: How was the option of confirming transactions done technically, that is, what happened after clicking to confirm the creation of a new LP position?

facts.a: cockpit path: the OPEN card's [Open] reads the pool on demand (slot0, liquidity) and opens the position window for a new position
facts.b: the window builds the mint with the same functions as the manual form (createPosition, prepareAddLiquidityTransaction)
facts.c: the window reads balance and allowance and asks for token approvals where needed
facts.d: each action switches the wallet network first and takes a fresh wallet client (getWalletClient) before the owner signs
facts.e: manual form path (AddLiquidity, 10.08): SDK amounts, approvals on exact amounts, eth_call simulation before the mint, slippage 0.1-1%

reference: The corpus records two paths. The one used for real positions is the cockpit: an OPEN proposal card has an [Open] button that reads the pool on demand (slot0 and liquidity over RPC) and opens the position window for a new position (no NFT yet). That window reads the wallet's balances and allowances, asks for token approvals where needed and builds the mint with the same functions as the manual add-liquidity form (createPosition and prepareAddLiquidityTransaction, rewritten on the Uniswap SDK on 10.08); before signing, each action switches the wallet to the right network and takes a fresh wallet client, and the owner signs in the wallet (Rabby). For the manual form (AddLiquidity, rewritten 10.08) the journal also records approvals on the exact amounts, an eth_call simulation of the mint before sending and slippage limited to 0.1 to 1%. After signing (fixes of 27.08, from the first real entry) the window waits for the receipt, re-reads balances and allowances, and after a successful mint closes with a toast confirming the new position.

Polish original: 'w jaki sposob technicznie byla zrealizowana opcja potwierdzania transakcji, czyli co dzialo sie po kliknieciu w potwierdzenie utworzenia nowej pozycji LP'.
